findings.claim: CI split does not survive cancellation: with `if: success() || failure()` a cancelled (timed-out/hung) crate step skips the remaining crate steps, so the exact hung-run scenario the split was built to diagnose still yields only the running step's log.

evidence.observation: Check job uses one step per crate (c3-core, c3, c3-cli), each `if: success() || failure()`; same pattern in the index-surreal job. In GitHub Actions a cancelled step makes `failure()` false for later steps, so they are skipped; `always()` (or `!cancelled()`) would be needed. Workspace members are exactly these three crates (Cargo.toml), so coverage is otherwise unchanged and the c3 index-surreal feature exists (crates/c3/Cargo.toml), i.e. failures still run all steps — only cancel skips.

findings.remedy: Use `if: always()` on the per-crate test steps (job outcome still reflects the failure/cancel).
findings.trigger: A test step is cancelled (45/30 min timeout, manual cancel, hung runner) instead of failing.
findings.verification: Cancel a run mid-test-step and confirm the later crate steps still execute and report.

findings.claim: Address table misses three IPv4-embedding IPv6 forms: Teredo 2001::/32, 6to4 2002::/16, and deprecated IPv4-compatible ::/96 (plus ISATAP). `to_ipv4_mapped` unwraps only ::ffff:0:0/96 and the code unwraps only the NAT64 /96 prefix; the other forms pass `is_public_address` as global even when the embedded IPv4 is private/loopback.

evidence.observation: NON_GLOBAL_V6 lists unspecified, loopback, 64:ff9b:1::/48, 100::/64, 2001:db8::/32, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, fec0::/10, ff00::/8 — no 2001::/32, no 2002::/16, no ::/96 compat range. is_public_address unwraps mapped and 64:ff9b::/96 only. Lookup-side (any-bad refuses) and peer-side checks plus the pinned-resolver are otherwise complete.

findings.remedy: Add 2001::/32 and 2002::/16 to the table (or unwrap their embedded IPv4 like NAT64) and refuse ::/96 compat addresses; add one row per range to the address tests.
findings.trigger: A name lookup or redirect hop answering a Teredo/6to4/compat address whose embedded IPv4 is non-global.
findings.verification: Unit-test is_public_address against 2001:0:<priv>:… , 2002:0a00:1:: and ::10.0.0.1; confirm currently returned as public.

findings.claim: The whole-entry fingerprint makes benign concurrent edits fatal to a good update: any added annotation key, inert ext field, or semantically-null JSON respelling between the gate snapshot and the smoke changes the SHA-256, so the smoke reports 'not run' and a passing engine update is rolled back / a swap abandoned.

evidence.observation: bound_roster refuses when entry_fingerprint(text) != fingerprint, where the fingerprint is SHA-256 of the canonical whole entry object; the swap flow binds fingerprint from the pre-smoke basis and smokes against it. Fail-closed by design, but the blast radius includes edits that change nothing the smoke executes.

findings.remedy: Keep fail-closed, but document that any roster edit during a pass holds that entry's update; optionally scope the fingerprint to executed fields (endpoint, auth, plan, key var, model, protection flags).
findings.trigger: Operator (or another session) edits the seated entry in any field while its pre/post smoke is in flight.
findings.verification: Edit an inert field of the seat between the two engine-update smokes in the e2e harness and observe rollback of a passing update.

findings.claim: A roster with no file path can never be smoked: fingerprint_now returns '' and bound_roster refuses an empty fingerprint unconditionally, so every engine update for such a roster is held on every pass with only a per-smoke line, instead of one loud refusal.

evidence.observation: fingerprint_now returns String::new when roster.path is empty; bound_roster errors when fingerprint.is_empty(). pick_target still returns a seat, so the pass proceeds to a smoke that cannot run.

findings.remedy: Return None from pick_target (or abort the engine step loudly) when the fingerprint is empty for a file-backed expectation.
findings.trigger: Maintain runs against a roster with empty `path` (tests, embedded use).
findings.verification: Call pick_target on a file-less roster and run_smoke; confirm perpetual 'not run' Fail rather than a single clear refusal.

findings.claim: An explicit 'no fixed price' marker bypasses the cross-major price hold: list_price keeps only positive finite numbers, so OpenRouter's "-1" (router, no fixed price) and "0" become 'no price', and price_hold returns None — the swap proceeds with no announcement, in the direction (unknown cost) the hold exists to catch.

evidence.observation: list_price drops '-1'/'0'/non-numeric (positive-finite filter); price_hold fires only when a source prices BOTH ids and the ratio exceeds 2. Documented intent covers 'without prices for both ids', but '-1' is affirmative unknown-price, not missing data.

findings.remedy: Treat an explicit '-1' on either side as unknown-price and hold/announce the cross-major swap (keep '0'/free seating).
findings.trigger: Catalog prices the seated id but marks the higher-major candidate '-1' (or vice versa).
findings.verification: Feed parse_catalog a candidate with pricing {prompt:'-1'} and confirm price_hold is None and the swap proceeds.

Q1. No passing path found for the listed forms: the table covers 0/8, 10/8, 100.64/10, 127/8, 169.254/16, 172.16/12, 192.0.0.0/24, docs ×3, 192.88.99/24, 192.168/16, 198.18/15, 224/4, 240/4 + broadcast, and IPv6 ::, ::1, 64:ff9b:1::/48, 100::/64, 2001:db8::/32, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, fec0::/10, ff00::/8 (`env.rs:325-357`); mapped/NAT64-/96 are unwrapped to their IPv4 (`env.rs:375-386`); lookup refuses on ANY bad address and the peer of every hop is checked (`env.rs:309-321,483-485`); the pinned resolver removes lookup→connect TOCTOU (`env.rs:215-222`). Residual: Teredo 2001::/32, 6to4 2002::/16 and compat ::/96 are neither listed nor unwrapped (finding #2, note).

Q2. No other client: engine/endpoint lists, catalogs, pages and installer/marker fetches all go through `Env::http_get` → `hop_agent` with `try_proxy_from_env(false)` (`env.rs:204-222`); key-carrying endpoint lists additionally use `Redirects::Never`. `run`/`run_clean` children intentionally keep proxy (installer needs it). Deadline: lookup-then-leftover-connect is correctly sequenced (`env.rs:242-268`); no retries; body bounded by hop timeout plus per-chunk deadline checks. Only the documented leaked lookup thread can outlive the deadline.

Q3. Fingerprint (`smoke.rs:76-93`): covers every value of the entry via canonical JSON, so no in-entry edit is invisible; out-of-entry edits are irrelevant (one-entry bound roster). Benign concurrent edits cause refusal → rollback of good updates (finding #3); empty-path rosters never smoke (finding #4). Per-turn proof (`smoke.rs:840-867`): evidence bound between each turn's own boundaries, unpaired boundaries and missing terminals are unproven, breach (shown surface) fails — no passing-without-evidence shape found in the check. Legitimate-but-refused: any concurrent entry touch, including inert fields.

Q4. Pairing is per-source and per-field with same-vendor seated entry (`models.rs:432-453`); zero/`-1`/missing become no-price (verified in `web.rs:371-386`), so an explicit `-1` bypasses the hold (finding #5, note). Lab token (`models.rs:730-773`, `plan.rs:115-132`): requires token≠rest labs to match maker/plan/host lab AND a same-maker catalog slug; mismatch shapes I constructed fail closed to 'no match' (smoke then decides). Spelling: alias view rekeys ids+dates+prices consistently (`models.rs:780-808`), invalid respellings fall back to catalog spelling (safe: no successor). Known `openai::gpt-6.2-sol` successor seating is brief-admitted, not re-reported.

Q5. No: dash form requires `anthropic/` slug + trusted source + differing id + `is_published_claude_shape` (family + 1–2 numeric groups; `claude.rs:180-182`). `claude-3.5-sonnet`, 3-group versions, unknown families yield nothing. Endpoint/engine lists never publish. Only an operator-declared `public:true` source can publish new names — the documented trust model.

Q6. No: the hook is read only inside the `mode_on()` branch (`mod.rs:465-468`); production reads the process table. Exact, case-insensitive engine-name match — cannot spill to other engines.

Q7. Failures do not hide later steps (`success() || failure()` runs them; job still fails). But a *cancelled* (hung/timed-out) step skips the rest (finding #1, minor) — defeating the split's purpose. Otherwise identical coverage (3 workspace members; `c3/index-surreal` exists).
